To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

all three severe plastic deformation methods, rotary swaging, equal channel angular pressing and multiaxal deformation, lead to the formation in the WE43 Mg-Y-Nd-Zre ultrafine-grained (UFG) structure, which results in strengthening of the WE43.

all three modes of severe plastic deformations (RS, ECAP, and MAD) result in ultrafine-grained microstructure, strengthening, and improvement of the corrosion and biocompatibility properties of the WE43 Mg alloy.
all three SPD modes (RS, ECAP, and MAD) are effective in strengthening the WE43 alloy, while ECAP and MAD are also capable of improving its ductility.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effect of severe plastic processing of WE43 Mg alloy on its structure and properties, including biodegradation and biocompatibility, which makes it possible to use this alloy in biomedical engineering.
the study of the structure, mechanical and corrosion properties, and biocompatibilty of WE43 Mg alloy after different modes of SPD.
a new approach to the development of biodegradable magnesium-based materials with enhanced properties.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ultrafine-grained WE43 alloy produced by ECAP and MAD is a promising bioresorbable biomaterial with a high mechanical performance and good biocompatibility.
all the three modes of SPD can be used for the production of bioresorbable WE43 alloy.
all three SPD modes can be used for strengthening of WE43 alloy and that MAD and ECAP, in comparison with RS, are preferable for improving the biocompatibility and decelerating biodegradation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the WE43 alloy after ECAP and MAD is promising for applications as bioabsorbable material.
the ultrafine-grained WE43 alloy has a high strength, good corrosion resistance, and good biocompatibility.
the WE43 alloy can be strengthened by SPD and that the strengthening is accompanied by the improvement of the biocompatibility.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the WE43 alloy is promising for biomedical applications, and its mechanical and biological properties can be tailored by SPD.
the ECAP and MAD treatments are more effective for the WE43 alloy than RS in terms of microstructure refinement and strengthening of the material.
ECAP and MAD can be used to improve the mechanical properties of Mg-Y-Nd-Zn alloys without compromising their biocompatibility.
